intent: Maintain the 7-sensor symmetric array with 0.016 m sensor size and 0.16 m wheel track to improve lateral line coverage and stability. Expect reduced line loss events, lower rms error, and smoother steering, especially on the challenging slalom track. This setup provides the integrator a stable, well-covered sensing platform to refine control and improve completion rates.
rationale: Iteration 3's addition of two sensors to form a 7-sensor symmetric array improved lateral coverage but did not eliminate line loss events or enable finishes on the slalom track. Steering oscillation remains moderate, and control effort is high, indicating the controller struggles with stability and line tracking. To address this, I maintain the 7-sensor layout with symmetric spacing at y=0.04 m and extend lateral coverage to ±0.06 m, preserving sensor size at 0.016 m for coverage and noise tolerance. Wheel track remains at 0.16 m to balance stability and maneuverability. Mass is kept at 0.7 kg to retain acceleration benefits. I keep wheel radius at 0.035 m and body dimensions unchanged to isolate sensor geometry effects. I expect this configuration to reduce line loss events and rms error further, improve line detection in sharp curves, and help reduce steering oscillation by providing richer sensor input. The integrator can then tune PID gains to leverage this improved sensing. Feedback requested includes completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, max_error, steering_oscillation, and control_effort to evaluate tracking quality and control effort.
